findings.text: Comparing via UnixNano() overflows int64 for times outside roughly 1678–2262, and the result is undefined there. For example, the zero time.Time{} (year 1) against time.Now() can compare wrongly, so Greater/Less assertions pass or fail incorrectly. Compare with Time.Compare, or with Before/After/Equal, instead.

obj2 is converted to time.Time without checking its type. If obj1 is a time.Time and obj2 is a different struct, for example struct{}{}, the callers only check that the kinds match. Convert then panics instead of returning a failed comparison. Check obj2Value.CanConvert(timeType), or require obj1 and obj2 to have the same type, before converting.

1.reason: The patch only checks obj1Value.CanConvert(timeType), and callers such as compareTwoValues in testify only check that the reflect kinds match (both Struct), so a non-convertible obj2 like struct{}{} reaches obj2Value.Convert(timeType) and panics; this is a separate defect from the UnixNano overflow (the context directory was missing, so the caller check comes from upstream testify, not this workspace).
